# avahi / fuzz-strlst

avahi's own fuzz target `fuzz-strlst` ([source](source/fuzz-strlst.c), unmodified), one of the targets OSS-Fuzz builds, over avahi (avahi/avahi at b1a83592).

Checks 5 properties (listed below); the first, a round trip: parse -> serialize -> parse: avahi_string_list_equal(original, reparsed) (element sizes and bytes, in order). A re-parse FAILURE is not flagged (goto finish).

## How this program differs from what OSS-Fuzz runs
- Linked against avahi at commit b1a83592.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the harness one to four times and prints each return value.

## What the harness checks
- avahi_string_list_to_string of a parsed TXT string list is valid UTF-8 ([lines 46-47](source/fuzz-strlst.c#L46-L47)): assert(); confirmed in the binary.
- bytes written by avahi_string_list_serialize equal the size the sizing call reported ([lines 57-58](source/fuzz-strlst.c#L57-L58)): assert(); confirmed in the binary.
- parse -> serialize -> parse: avahi_string_list_equal(original, reparsed) (element sizes and bytes, in order). A re-parse FAILURE is not flagged (goto finish) ([lines 60-64](source/fuzz-strlst.c#L60-L64)): assert(); not confirmed in the binary.
- avahi_string_list_copy(a) is avahi_string_list_equal to a ([lines 67-71](source/fuzz-strlst.c#L67-L71)): assert(); not confirmed in the binary.

A failure of any of the checks at lines 46-47 and lines 57-58 ends the process with a status that the halts statements below that name them exclude, so a proof of one of those statements implies them on every input it covers. No statement here proves the other checks.

## Statements ([Statements.v](Statements.v), [Characterise.v](Characterise.v), [Distribution.v](Distribution.v))

| statement | in one line | status |
|---|---|---|
| `plain_halts` | on every input on which the plain build is never refused memory for exceeding 16 GiB (a premise), it exits with status 0 or 2; so the checks at lines 46-47 and lines 57-58 above hold | open |
| `ubsan_halts` | on every input on which the UBSan build is never refused memory for exceeding 16 GiB (a premise), it exits with status 0 or 2; so the checks at lines 46-47 and lines 57-58 above hold | open |
| `ubsan_agrees` | on every input on which the plain build is never refused memory for exceeding 16 GiB (a premise): neither build reaches an error and both have the same set of observable behaviours; UBSan never fires | open |
| `ubsan_disagrees_at_most` | P[plain and UBSan disagree] <= b under [Distribution.v](Distribution.v) | open (best proved b: none) |
| `ubsan_agreement_decidable` | some program decides exactly the inputs where plain and UBSan agree | open |

## Builds
Static riscv64 Linux programs, compiled for RV64G and run as `<file> <input-file>`; `oft fetch avahi` downloads the published ones and checks each against its SHA-256.

| build | file | bytes | sha256 |
|---|---|---:|---|
| plain | `fuzz-strlst.plain` | 50,544 | `23cf75bc8261e68fcdad66c4343b7160b34adb14d96adff3f873a51c21101d4a` |
| ubsan | `fuzz-strlst.ubsan` | 51,192 | `eb81abc429a30f2b3da357ce1faf07390d172740b16e6d41299669d37f3dc042` |

Each build also links code that no sanitizer instruments, as its link recorded it. A statement about a sanitizer build covers that code only as uninstrumented code: ASan checks no load or store made inside it, and UBSan inserts no check there.

- plain: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
